subject: Data localization assurance and interim cross-region handoff procedures
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ian Rogers <ian.rogers@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data locality: PHI scope and cross-region handling—initial questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the brief intro yesterday. As we start the security review for our pilot, a few early questions so we can map to Acme Health's data localization requirements (PHI scope):

- Can Redwood commit to processing customer data exclusively within the US for our environment, including all inference, embeddings, and model caching?
- If you offer a "region affinity" or pinning option, what are the exact failure modes where data might leave the pinned region (e.g., DR failover, autoscaling, maintenance)?
- What is the maximum duration that any transient cross-region sync or replication may take place (we need a numeric upper bound to show our compliance team)?
- Please attach the full subprocessors roster and indicate which operate inside vs outside the US. Also share KMS/HSM options and whether keys can be customer-managed.

We attached a short SOW and the vendor security questionnaire to this thread. Can you please put together acceptance criteria we can present to our GRC and Procurement teams?

Appreciate a concise list of measurable guarantees and an outline of the mutual action plan (timeline for documentation & DPA addendum).

Best,

Lara Chen
Director, Security & Privacy
Acme Health
Attachments: acme-sow.docx (docx), security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality: PHI scope and cross-region handling—initial questions

Lara — thanks for the clear list. I wanted to give an operational-first answer and propose a short acceptance checklist you can take to GRC. Below is a concise breakdown; Marcus and Monica are looped in for technical + legal detail.

Summary (short):
- Redwood can operate in a US-only pinned deployment for your account.
- We offer two modes: Soft Affinity (preferred for autoscale & cost) and Hard Pin (stronger contractual guarantee).
- Transient cross-region activity is limited to explicit failover windows; proposed operational upper bound: up to 6 hours for KV/cache synchronization and up to 24 hours for longer background replication during sustained outage (see Marcus' note below for telemetry).
- Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments (bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS & GCP CMEK connections).
- We'll provide a signed DPA addendum for hard pin that enumerates subprocessors and the narrow exceptions for failover.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
1) Environment must be deployed as a US pinned instance and configured with customer KMS keys.
2) Any cross-region replication must be telemetered and auditable (we will provide event logs and a weekly digest for the first 90 days).
3) Maximum transient sync windows: KV/cache sync <= 6 hours; longer replication (indexing/backup) <= 24 hours only during sustained region outage and only after escalation.
4) Subprocessor roster provided and redlined in the DPA addendum; any new subprocessor outside the US requires 30-day notice and written approval.

Attachments: initial-pin-proposal.pdf (pdf) — contains a brief SLA/operational runbook and suggested DPA language.

Can you confirm these criteria are sufficient for Acme's GRC? If yes, I'll loop in Legal to prepare draft addendum and send the subprocessor roster (Marcus to attach).

Thanks,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality: PHI scope and cross-region handling—initial questions

Lara / Tessa — quick technical addendum to the acceptance criteria so your engineers can validate the design. TL;DR: we can meet the acceptance criteria with the stated upper bounds, with a couple of measurable caveats.

Operational notes (technical):
- Hard Pin vs Soft Affinity: Hard Pin ties customer workloads to a dedicated VPC/region and disables background scheduler-driven cross-region relocation. Soft Affinity prefers the region but allows proactive placement for capacity.
- Failover flows:
  * Hot failover (node-level): short-lived connection reroutes may cause ephemeral KV cache misses; those misses are handled in-region where possible but may trigger background cache fill from a peer region for up to 6 hours.
  * DR relocation (region-level outage): in a sustained outage we pre-warm a fallback pool in a paired region. Background replication of model shards and metadata can take up to 24 hours in extreme cases; we require a manual escalation to proceed with cross-region replication.
- Telemetry & evidence: every cross-region transfer will be logged with event-level metadata (timestamp, object id, size, originating region, destination region). We can provide a machine-readable audit dump (CSV) for the time window you request plus human-readable summary.
- Subprocessors: attached roster lists AWS, GCP, S3 replication partners, and a small set of monitoring vendors. Rows include country of operation and whether data-at-rest is replicated outside the US.

Operational constraints you should be aware of:
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for Private and Dedicated deployments only. Hosted accounts can be configured with customer keys for encryption-at-rest but certain ephemeral caches still use service-managed keys for performance reasons; those caches are encrypted and logged.
- Short-lived metadata: retention of ephemeral KV cache logs is 7 days by default; we can increase retention for compliance at additional cost and with a retention SLA.

Attachment: subprocessor-roster.csv (csv)

Let us know the format Acme prefers for the audit dump and what retention window you'd like us to hold event logs for review.

—Marcus
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality: PHI scope and cross-region handling—initial questions

Tessa / Marcus — thanks, that level of detail is exactly what our GRC needs. A few quick next asks so we can close internally: 

1) Please confirm you will provide a draft DPA addendum (we'd like the hard pin language and the 30-day subprocessor notice included).
2) We need a signed mutual action plan with milestones: DPA draft, legal review, SOC evidence, final acceptance testing. Can you propose dates? Our preferred timeline is: DPA draft by 2027-06-25, legal review complete by 2027-07-09, pilot acceptance test week of 2027-07-19.
3) For audit purposes please provide a short how-to for requesting the machine-readable cross-region audit dump and confirm retention options; we prefer 90 days of event logs.

If you can provide the DPA draft and the subprocessor CSV in the next week, we'll slot this into our procurement cycle and get DocuSign moving. Attaching a sample MMP (mutual action plan) we use as a template.

Thanks again — we are excited to push the pilot forward.

Best,

Lara
Director, Security & Privacy
Acme Health
Attachments: Acme-MMP-template.pdf (pdf)
